blocos.titulo: Quantity and support tables for the genitive plural
blocos.explicacao: The big application: QUANTITY. Certain words of quantity take the genitive. The most important are in the table below. Notice: all of them take the genitive, always. Examples in sentences follow. The rule: мно́го, ма́ло, немно́го, ско́лько, сто́лько and не́сколько always take the genitive. And is it the genitive singular or plural? It depends on the word. Uncountable words (са́хар, вода́, вре́мя) → genitive singular (мно́го са́хара, ма́ло вре́мени). Countable words (кни́га, стол, дом) → genitive plural (мно́го книг, ма́ло столо́в). It is the same split English makes between "much" and "many": if the thing is countable, plural; if uncountable, singular. blocos.titulo: Common mistakes and sentences in the genitive plural
blocos.explicacao: The mistakes English speakers WILL make with the genitive plural. Mistake 1: using the singular after «нет» when the thing is plural. Wrong: У меня́ нет кни́ги. (singular, but you meant several books) Right: У меня́ нет книг. (plural) You learned the genitive singular in lesson 27 and tend to use it everywhere. But when the thing is plural, the genitive is plural. Mistake 2: adding -ОВ to a feminine in -а (instead of dropping the ending). Wrong: У меня́ нет ма́мов / кни́гов. Right: У меня́ нет мам / книг. Mistake 3: forgetting the -ОВ on a hard masculine. Wrong: У меня́ нет стол. Right: У меня́ нет столо́в. A hard masculine takes -ОВ. Mistake 4: using -ОВ on soft or sibilant stems that need -ЕЙ. Wrong: У меня́ нет учи́телов / врачо́в. Right: У меня́ нет учителе́й / враче́й. Mistake 5: forgetting the fleeting vowel. Wrong: У меня́ нет ко́шк. Right: У меня́ нет ко́шек. The fleeting vowel is obligatory when the stem ends in two consonants. Mistake 6: mixing up the number rules. Wrong: У меня́ пять кни́ги. Right: У меня́ пять книг. 5+ takes the genitive PLURAL, not the singular. It is one of the most confused rules. Mistake 7: forgetting that 2, 3, 4 take the genitive SINGULAR. Wrong: У меня́ две книг. Right: У меня́ две кни́ги. 2, 3, 4 take the genitive SINGULAR, not the plural. It is the opposite of the previous mistake. Mistake 8: forgetting that 1 goes with the nominative. Wrong: У меня́ одна́ кни́ги. Right: У меня́ одна́ кни́га. 1 goes with the nominative singular. It is the only number that does not take the genitive. Mistake 9: using the wrong gender with the number 2. Wrong: два кни́ги. Right: две кни́ги. Два is masculine/neuter. Две is feminine. Кни́га is feminine, so две. Mistake 10: forgetting the genitive after БЕЗ, ДЛЯ, ДО, ИЗ, ОТ, У. Wrong: без са́хар. Right: без са́хара. Wrong: для ма́ма. Right: для ма́мы. All the prepositions of the genitive take the genitive, always. Full sentences with the genitive plural. Here are real sentences.

blocos.titulo: Closing the essential grammar and summary of the genitive
blocos.explicacao: A final word of reassurance: you have finished the essential grammar. Now a pause. Listen to what I am about to say. You have finished the essential grammar of Russian. You have now seen all 6 cases: STEP 1: Nominative, the case of the subject. STEP 2: Accusative, the case of the action. STEP 3: Prepositional, the case of place. STEP 4: Dative, the case of things that happen to you. STEP 5: Instrumental, the case of the extensions of the body and of "with". STEP 6: Genitive, the case of possession, origin and negation. You already know the alphabet. The gender of nouns. The gender of adjectives. Verbs in the present, past and future. Personal pronouns, possessives and demonstratives. Numbers. The main prepositions. And here is the truth nobody tells you: the hard part of Russian is over. The learner's mistake is to think the advanced stage is the hard one. In Russian the hard part is the basic structure, because it is abstract, full of rules and full of exceptions. You faced that part and you won. What comes next is not harder, it is richer. After the genitive, Russian opens up into vocabulary (thousands of new words), idioms (learning to talk like a Russian), culture (understanding why Russians say what they say) and immersion (reading books, listening to music, watching films, talking with Russians). All of that is much easier than grammar, because it is intuitive, cultural and alive. You already have the structure. Now you build the house. One thing is left: practice. Read, listen, speak, write, every day, even if only for 15 minutes, because structure only consolidates with use. Summary table: the genitive plural.

Ordinals are adjectives: they agree with the noun. Masculine: первый, второй, третий...; feminine: первая, вторая, третья...; neuter: первое, второе, третье.... «Третий» is special (третья, третье, третьи). To give the date, use the ordinal in the NEUTER and the month in the GENITIVE: «первое мая» (1 May, "the first of May"). To say "on" a date, the ordinal also goes into the genitive: «первого мая» (on 1 May). Uses: floor («на третьем этаже»), order («второй урок»).

exemplos.pt: Today is the first of May.
My birthday is on the tenth of June.
